title: Reduce GPU footprint via transient-activation-striping and elastic-scratch-tiering
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Large decoder-style models still incur high transient GPU workspace usage from activations and temporary scratch buffers even after activation checkpointing. This PR introduces two complementary runtime mechanisms to reduce peak GPU working set: 1) transient activation striping: partition activation checkpoints into small, cache-friendly stripes evictable to a compact per-GPU reserved buffer and rehydrated on-demand; and 2) elastic scratch tiering: classify scratch allocations into fast local slab and slower shared pool (spill to host or remote device memory) with an adaptive placement policy driven by live sequence-length distributions. Design summary and rationale are included below. The implementation aims to be opt-in behind flags for canary rollout and compatible with existing KV-cache and continuous-batching flows. Key outcomes: up to 32% reduction in peak device memory for mixed-length workloads, median 6% end-to-end latency increase in high-concurrency tails compensated by improved batching density and fewer OOMs, and smoother scale-up behavior for Dedicated pools. See benchmarks and rollout plan at the bottom.
commit_summaries: Add transient activation striping runtime module and allocator glue
Implement elastic scratch tier with slab and shared-spill strategies
Integrate striping with activation checkpoint read/write paths and KV-cache consistency checks
Add adaptive placement controller driven by sequence-length histograms
Add unit and integration tests + microbenchmarks for mixed-length decoding
Docs: runtime flags, rollout steps, and observability metrics
files_changed: runtime/allocator/transient_striping.cpp - new striped checkpoint store and allocator hooks (approx 420 lines)
runtime/allocator/elastic_scratch.cc - slab + shared-tier implementation and spill policy (approx 310 lines)
runtime/allocator/allocator.h - new flags and APIs for tiered allocation
runtime/inference/checkpointing.cc - integrate stripe read/write and async prefetch
runtime/inference/kv_cache_manager.cc - add hooks to pin/unpin stripes during KV compaction
runtime/scheduler/placement_controller.cc - adaptive policy using per-model seq-length histograms
tools/debug/inspect_stripes.py - debug helper to dump stripe placement across GPUs
runtime/telemetry/emitters.cc - emit new histogram telemetry for sequence lengths
review_comments: Ethan Martinez (2024-09-15): High-level: neat idea. Please add more detail on correctness when stripes are evicted mid-inference; we need guarantees the KV-cache doesn't reference evicted slices.
Priya Nair (2024-09-15): Reply: Added explicit pin/unpin semantics in kv_cache_manager and a lightweight checksum on stripes to detect stale references. See allocator.h comments and unit tests added.
Lena Cho (2024-09-18): Question: did you measure the spill latency when elastic tier moves scratch to host? Concerned about tail latency impact for short sequences.

Priya Nair (2024-09-18): Reply: Yes — microbenchmarks included. For short sequences we avoid spill by biasing placement to slab; controller learns workload and only spills for low-probability long sequences. Results in docs/benchmarks show median impact ~+6% latency at 99th percentile improvement in OOM rate.

Michael Bauer (2024-09-22): Request changes: prefer exposing a telemetry gauge for active stripe count per request and avoiding global locks in allocator hot path. Also asked for simplified API to toggle per-model policy.

Priya Nair (2024-09-23): Addressed: added stripe_count gauge, replaced heavy spinlock with per-GPU lock-free freelist for common path, and exposed per-model policy in config.py. Added tests for concurrency.
Lena Cho (2024-09-26): Approval: verified memory reduction on internal mixed-length corpus and smoke-tested Dedicated pool. Leaving a thumbs-up.
Ethan Martinez (2024-09-29): Approved after minor nits fixed (doc wording + CI flake fix).
CI Bot (2024-09-30): Integration tests flaked once on macOS build; reran and all checks passed.
release_notes: Introduce transient activation striping and elastic scratch tiering to reduce GPU peak working set by up to ~32% for mixed-length decoding workloads. Opt-in via runtime flags; recommended canary rollout. Impact: fewer OOMs and lower Dedicated pool scale-ups at the cost of small tail latency trade-offs for extreme configurations.
